video.title: You Can Feel This - Here's How

classification.reason: The coach gives explicit cues and execution intents for the player's internal control system: drive your shoulders forward while intending to pull or accelerate the hip backwards to stretch the fascial chain.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you intend to pull your hip back when it visibly rotates forward in the swing?
problem.definition: Players often misunderstand the biomechanics and control system of pelvic rotation, trying actively to drive the right hip forward through the shot, which prevents the fascial stretch that accelerates the shoulders.

symptoms.description: The hips and shoulders rotate forward together without counter-twist tension.
The feeling of fascial tension yanking the hip backward and shoulder forward is completely missing.

causes.statement: The connecting fascial and muscular line between hip and shoulder exerts equal tension flinging the shoulder forward while pulling the hip backward.
Using the cue to push the hip forward causes the brain to avoid building stretch tension so the hip can move freely with the shoulders.
The pelvis fires forward at the start of the swing to load maximum stretch tension onto the line that decelerates and pulls it backwards.
The hip decelerates via backward acceleration from fascial tension rather than reversing its visible forward motion.

angles.summary: Demonstrating the hip-to-shoulder fascial connection with an elastic corkscrew model showing anchors pulling in opposite directions.
Clarifying that instructing players to drive the right hip forward prevents them from stretching the torso against the shoulder.
Explaining that human perception senses tension and acceleration rather than absolute positional motion.

solutions.summary: Cue yourself to drive the shoulders forward while pulling the hips back to create stretch tension.

ban_conflict.note: Actively driving the hip forward disables the counter-tension needed to fling the shoulders.

solutions.summary: Check for the distinct moment where the pelvis feels yanked backwards while the shoulders are yanked forward.
Focus on feeling the pelvis under tension getting pulled backwards as the shoulders accelerate.
Frame your movement intent as desiring to increase the tension that pulls the shoulders forward and pelvis back.
